extracted.intended_audience: legislators, political theorists, and citizens interested in democratic governance and public morals
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for lawmakers and public-minded citizens in democratic societies on how to preserve moral/spiritual health, sustain freedom and industry, and balance private welfare with civic duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator must discern and act on natural inclinations of the people
rubrics_metrics.description: "The whole art of the legislator is correctly to discern beforehand these natural inclinations of communities of men, in order to know whether they should be assisted, or whether it may not be necessary to check them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators should study the predispositions and tastes of their society and decide case-by-case whether to encourage or restrain them; this is framed as a central craft of legislation rather than imposing one-size-fits-all rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise and sustain spiritual and moral sentiments among citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: "It should therefore be the unceasing object of the legislators of democracies, and of all the virtuous and enlightened men who live there, to raise the souls of their fellow-citizens, and keep them lifted up towards heaven...to diffuse the love of the infinite, a sense of greatness, and a love of pleasures not of earth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators and civic leaders should actively promote devotion to higher, non-material ends (religion, love of the infinite, lofty tastes) as a corrective to excessive materialism in democratic societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve established religious belief in democracies rather than disrupt it
rubrics_metrics.description: “When therefore any religion has struck its roots deep into a democracy, beware lest you disturb them; but rather watch it carefully... Seek not to supersede the old religious opinions of men by new ones; lest in the passage from one faith to another, the soul being left for a while stripped of all belief, the love of physical gratifications should grow upon it and fill it wholly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid policies or interventions that uproot entrenched religious beliefs; changes in dominant faiths can leave a moral vacuum that encourages materialism. The preferable approach is cautious stewardship rather than abrupt replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose materialism and doctrines that deny the immaterial soul
rubrics_metrics.description: "If amongst the opinions of a democratic people any of those pernicious theories exist which tend to inculcate that all perishes with the body, let men by whom such theories are professed be marked as the natural foes of such a people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the spread of materialist doctrines as a political and moral hazard in democracies: identify, criticize, and resist ideas that reduce human nature to mere matter because they amplify risks of social enervation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not substitute official philosophies or state religions for natural belief
rubrics_metrics.description: "I am no believer in the prosperity, any more than in the durability, of official philosophies; and as to state religions... they always, sooner or later, become fatal to the Church."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While religion and moral sentiment should be supported, imposing an official state ideology or church is discouraged; state-enforced doctrines often backfire and harm genuine religious life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect freedom because it is necessary for productive industry
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is therefore a close bond and necessary relation between these two elements--freedom and productive industry... Freedom, in these ages, is therefore especially favorable to the production of wealth; nor is it difficult to perceive that despotism is especially adverse to the same result."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should safeguard political and economic freedoms to foster commerce and industry; minute, meddling despotism undermines the genius of commerce and productive pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent citizens from neglecting public duties due to private pursuits
rubrics_metrics.description: When citizens engross themselves in private business and see public duties as "a troublesome annoyance," the place of government is left "unfilled" and the road to usurpation is opened by ambitious individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and enable civic participation (voting, attending public meetings, public service). Civic neglect is identified as a key vulnerability that can permit factional or individual usurpation of power; policy and culture should counteract that tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn against trading freedom for mere public tranquillity
rubrics_metrics.description: "A nation which asks nothing of its government but the maintenance of order is already a slave at heart--the slave of its own well-being... A nation which asks nothing of its government but the maintenance of order is already a slave at heart."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public tranquillity is a legitimate goal but insufficient as the sole demand on government. Citizens and leaders should resist surrendering substantive liberties in exchange for stability or material comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and temper excessive taste for physical gratifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The love of physical gratifications in democracies can become "tenacious, exclusive, universal" and while often moderate it can "enervate" the soul if it absorbs people wholly; democratic tastes for small comforts can close out loftier pursuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that material improvement and comforts are natural in democracies but require cultural and institutional checks (education, religion, civic virtues) to prevent ennervation, loss of higher faculties, and weakening of public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious when popular appetite for wealth outpaces education and experience of freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: "When the taste for physical gratifications amongst such a people has grown more rapidly than their education and their experience of free institutions, the time will come when men are carried away, and lose all self-restraint..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If economic appetites advance faster than civic education and experience, democratic self-restraint can erode. Policies should seek to align economic opportunity with civic education and institutions that cultivate capacity for self-government.
